findings.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:623 — Repeated fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v) calls copy the entire accumulated SQLite ID list on each iteration, causing quadratic allocation and copying for large cleanup batches.

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:535 — Normal cleanup operations unconditionally emit error logs for successful deletions and empty batches, producing false error signals on every cleanup cycle.

pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go:77 — Reducing the shared cleanup ticker from ten minutes to one minute runs every job in the loop ten times as often, increasing database and other cleanup work independently of annotation batching.

goldens.comment: The code uses Error log level for what appears to be debugging information. This will pollute error logs in production. Consider using Debug or Info level instead.

The cleanup job ticker was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, which can lead to increased database load and contention due to more frequent execution of cleanup tasks. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with performance expectations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:623 — Repeated fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v) calls copy the entire accumulated SQLite ID list on each iteration, causing quadratic allocation and copying for large cleanup batches.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the code at lines 620-623 uses repeated string concatenation with fmt.Sprintf in a loop: `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)`. This pattern does cause quadratic allocation because each iteration creates a new string copying all previous content. While this is a real performance concern for large batches (the test case uses 32767 batch size), it's not a bug that causes incorrect behavior - the code will still function correctly, just inefficiently. A strings.Builder would be more appropriate. This is a valid performance concern but not a correctness bug.
